comments.body:
THE COMMENT CEILING IS NOW ESTABLISHED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES. AC4 can be satisfied by DOCUMENTING
PROVENANCE rather than by measurement or by marking the binding UNVERIFIED — and the working
hypothesis that motivated the doubt was REFUTED, which changes what this story should do.

THE HYPOTHESIS I ASKED TO BE TESTED, AND ITS REFUTATION. I suspected 32767 was the limit for TEXT
CUSTOM FIELDS, misapplied to comments, with the real comment body stored as a CLOB and effectively
unbounded. The storage half is CORRECT — jiraaction.actionbody is type 'extremely-long' in
entitymodel.xml (LONGTEXT on MySQL, CLOB on Oracle; Atlassian's Jira 7.9.2 schema PDF). But the
column is NOT the binding constraint: enforcement happens at the APPLICATION layer before the insert
(CommentBodyCharacterLimitExceededException / IssueFieldsCharacterLimitExceededException).

DECISIVE SOURCE — Jira's own jpm.xml, which defines advanced-settings defaults:
    key: jira.text.field.character.limit
    description: 'The maximum number of characters to be entered for a single field.
                  Affects Description, Environment, Comments and Text custom fields.
                  0 means unlimited.'
    default-value: 32767
So Comments and Text custom fields are governed by ONE property and therefore THE SAME NUMBER, by
design. They were never two limits that got conflated. Corroborated by JRASERVER-28519
(Resolved/Fixed, fix versions 6.4.1 / 7.0.0): 'starting with JIRA 7.0 and Cloud,
jira.text.field.character.limit will be set to 32767 by default.' Jira 6.x jpm.xml carries the same
key with default 0 and already listed Comments in scope. The DC admin page 'Configuring advanced
settings' confirms the property, its field scope, 0 = unlimited and max 2147483647 — but note it
does NOT state the default; the default comes from jpm.xml and JRASERVER-28519.

SO: 32767 IS THE CORRECT DC COMMENT CEILING FOR STOCK JIRA >= 7.0. Binding comment and description
to one constant is, unusually, structurally faithful to how DC actually works. This story must NOT
change the limit, and must NOT mark it UNVERIFIED — it is verified, and verified as correct for the
default case. AC4 is met by recording THIS provenance (the property name + JRASERVER-28519) at the
binding, replacing an assumption with a citation.

WHAT REMAINS A REAL DEFECT, IN THE SAME DIRECTION I SUSPECTED BUT BY A NARROWER PATH: on DC the
limit is ADMIN-CONFIGURABLE (0-2147483647) and rebar hardcodes the default. On an instance where an
admin raised it or set 0, rebar truncates comments Jira would have accepted in full. That is data
loss. It is documented and not rare — JRASERVER-64351 has 86 votes from people hitting the ceiling.
Filed separately rather than folded in here, per this story's own scope rule that a limit/behaviour
change is its own ticket.

TWO SECONDARY FINDINGS THE RESEARCH SURFACED, both latent traps rather than live bugs:
 1. THE CONSTANT ASSERTS A FALSE PROVENANCE. It is named WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT and lives in
    rich_text.py, and the comment at jira_family/rich_text.py:56-60 attributes the number to Cloud
    comment limits — which REVERSES the actual causality. On DC the number comes from
    jira.text.field.character.limit, which covers descriptions AND comments.
 2. sanitize_comment REUSES fit_outbound, THE DESCRIPTION FITTER. Behaviour is correct today because
    that fitter is a plain character truncation. But Cloud demonstrates exactly why the coupling is
    dangerous: Cloud's description fitter is ADF-SIZE-based (_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000 ADF chars,
    fitted empirically because text_to_adf inflates — a 32767-char description was observed
    serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars) and would be catastrophically wrong applied to comments. Any
    future change to the DC description fitter silently retargets comments.

WHY CLOUD HAS A SEPARATE comment_limits MODULE — this corrects an assumption in this ticket's
Context. It is NOT because Cloud's comment ceiling differs numerically from its description ceiling;
both derive from 32767. It is because the UNITS differ: Cloud comments are limited in PLAIN chars
(_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767, a hard non-configurable Cloud limit — JRACLOUD-63007 asking to make
it configurable was closed Won't Do) while Cloud descriptions are limited in ADF-SERIALIZED size. DC
has no ADF inflation, which is why ONE constant genuinely suffices there. So DC's single-constant
binding is not a shortcut Cloud avoided; it is correct for DC's actual text format.

FIELD COMPARISON (evidence that hardcoding is the norm, so this is hardening, not a defect class):
client libraries unanimously do NOT cap comments — pycontribs/jira, andygrunwald/go-jira (both cloud
and onpremise), go-jira CLI, atlassian-python-api all post the body verbatim; '32767' returns zero
hits in each. Sentry's jira_server client posts comments raw while explicitly truncating SUMMARY to
255 — so it considered field limits and guarded only summary. Application-level sync tools DO cap at
32767: carrier-io/dusty annotates its constant '# This is jira.text.field.character.limit default
value', an independent implementer tracing the number to the same property. RedHatQE/newa is the only
project found that branches on deployment type (32000 Cloud / 65000 Server) and even it guesses.
NO surveyed project queries the live limit. Atlassian's own JCMA truncates at 32767 and LOGS it
(MIG-1356), framing it as the Cloud target's limit and contrasting Server's configurability.

NOT ESTABLISHED, recorded so nobody assumes it: whether /rest/api/2/application-properties exposes
jira.text.field.character.limit to a non-admin PAT (any read-the-live-limit remediation depends on
this and must be TESTED, not assumed); whether the default is still 32767 in DC 9/10/11 (the jpm.xml
evidence read is from 7.1.9 — no primary source found for 10.x/11.x); and whether DC's REST v2
comment endpoint runs the same validator as the web UI (the exception class names imply shared
validation, but the DC REST comment resource was not read).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PLAN CERTIFIED after five review rounds. Recording what each round found, because every one named
something real and three of the five were MY errors — an implementer should trust this plan's
specifics rather than re-deriving them, and should know why they are worded so precisely.

ROUND 1-2 (the parametrization premise): the plan said DC convergence tests would be 'parametrized
alongside Cloud's where the mechanism is shared'. IMPOSSIBLE. Cloud's suites hardcode Cloud-only
internals — comment_limits.truncate_comment_body (test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py:154)
and ADF_PATH / _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT=32000 (test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py:31-34)
— which have no DC equivalent. Following it literally would have meant restructuring
incident-hardened Cloud tests, which this epic's own AC forbids. Now: SEPARATE DC files, the
default rather than a fallback.

ROUND 3 (the injection seam): a DC comment convergence test driven through
compute_outbound_mutations CANNOT reach DC's sanitizer. That function (outbound_differ.py:382-391)
takes outbound_mapper/inbound_mapper/links but NO sanitizer, and line 744 calls _diff_comments
WITHOUT forwarding one, so _resolve_sanitizer(None) -> select_backend(load_config()).sanitizer =
CLOUD. The test would have converged against Cloud's truncation while reporting DC convergence.
Fixed with no production change: _diff_comments already accepts sanitizer= (outbound_comments.py:167,
the ticket-21ca seam).

ROUND 4 — TWO FINDINGS, AND THE SECOND CAUGHT ME WRITING A TEST THAT CANNOT FAIL:
 (a) The OR-GUARD. outbound_differ.py:431 is
     'if outbound_mapper is None or inbound_mapper is None or links is None:' — so injecting ONLY
     outbound_mapper still fires the fallback and lets it resolve all three from config. All THREE
     must be injected. I had read that exact line in an earlier round and missed the implication.
 (b) MY 'DISCRIMINATING ASSERTION' WAS VACUOUS. I had required the comment test to assert DC's
     length boundary and truncation suffix to prove it used DC's path. But DC's
     WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound and Cloud's comment_limits.truncate_comment_body truncate at the
     SAME 32767 limit and append a BYTE-IDENTICAL suffix — ' … [truncated by reconciler]' at
     rich_text.py:69 and comment_limits.py:46 — and compute 'keep' the same way. So that assertion
     passes under EITHER sanitizer: precisely the tests-that-cannot-fail defect sibling ticket 2944
     exists to delete, which I introduced while enforcing a rule against it. The comment test now
     requires an IDENTITY/RECORDING proof that the injected DC sanitizer actually ran, and its
     mutation check targets the INJECTION rather than the value. The DESCRIPTION test keeps a
     value-based discriminator, which IS legitimate there because DC fits plain chars at 32767
     while Cloud fits ADF-SERIALIZED size at 32000 — those genuinely differ.

ROUND 5 (stale metadata): the file_impact I had declared still listed Cloud's EXISTING convergence
files with the reason 'extend Cloud coverage to DC' — contradicting the rewritten plan that says
those files stay BYTE-UNCHANGED. LESSON WORTH CARRYING: file_impact is REVIEWED MATERIAL, so the
'grep the whole document after editing' sweep must cover it too, not just the prose. Corrected to
the two NEW DC files plus the provenance-comment-only change to backend.py.

ALSO NOTE, from the earlier research comment: the comment CEILING itself is settled (32767 is the
documented default of jira.text.field.character.limit, which covers Comments as well as Description
— jpm.xml, JRASERVER-28519). Do NOT re-measure it and do NOT mark it UNVERIFIED; cite the
provenance at the binding. That it is admin-configurable is a separate ticket, 049e-9fac-a821-4ea2.

comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1234 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1234). Three files:
the two NEW DC convergence suites plus a provenance-COMMENT-only change to
adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py. Cloud's two convergence files are BYTE-UNCHANGED
(`git diff origin/main -- <both>` is empty). Module sizes: backend.py 350 -> 371 (cap 800);
new suites 234 and 241 LOC.

THE PLAN'S SPECIFICS ALL HELD — every one of the five rounds' findings was load-bearing in
practice, not just in principle. Recording the proofs.

DESCRIPTION SUITE — value discriminator, as the plan specified. All THREE of outbound_mapper=,
inbound_mapper= and links= bound to a real JiraDataCenterBackend over FakeTransport, via one
`_compute` helper so no call site can forget one. Landed description is exactly 32767 plain chars
and ends with " … [truncated by reconciler]"; pass 2 over that body plans zero description
updates; the local ticket keeps its full 40000 chars.

COMMENT SUITE — identity + recording, NOT value, exactly as round 4(b) required. `_diff_comments`
called DIRECTLY with `sanitizer=` and `inbound_mapper=` (both have their own config fallback).
The injected DC sanitizer is wrapped in a `RecordingSanitizer` that delegates every member
untouched (`__getattr__`) and records `fit_comment` calls. Two assertions carry the proof:
`recorder.wrapped is dc_backend.sanitizer` (identity) and `recorder.fit_comment_calls` non-empty
in BOTH passes (recording) — pass 2's zero-mutation result is only accepted if the injected
sanitizer actually ran, so it cannot be a zero produced by a bypass.

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE PLAN, because the first draft had a hole the plan did not name. Both
suites originally asserted the landed length against WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT — the very constant
under test. That made them SELF-CONSISTENT under a raised limit: mutating 32767 -> 400000 left the
convergence assertion green, because the fixture "Jira" stored whatever rebar sent. So each suite
now spells Jira's real ceiling as a LITERAL `_JIRA_TEXT_FIELD_CHARACTER_LIMIT = 32767` (a fact
about the instance, which does not move when rebar's constant does) and routes pass 1's output
through `_as_jira_would_store()` before pass 2. With that, a loosened limit makes CONVERGENCE
ITSELF fail, not merely a length assertion. Verified below (MUT B2b / B-neutralized).

MUTATION LEDGER — every verdict an AssertionError, never an AttributeError/ImportError:

MUTATED: dropped outbound_mapper=/inbound_mapper=/links= from the description suite's `_compute`
  (i.e. let the OR-guarded config fallback resolve the backend);
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes —
  "AssertionError: DC must fit the description to Jira's plain-character ceiling … assert 31887 ==
  32767". 31887 is Cloud's ADF fit. This is the round-3/round-4(a) finding reproduced exactly: the
  fallback resolves CLOUD and the cell would otherwise have been green while testing the wrong
  deployment.

MUTATED: dropped BOTH sanitizer= and inbound_mapper= from the comment suite's `_diff`;
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes —
  "AssertionError: The injected DC sanitizer was never consulted: _diff_comments fell back to
  select_backend(load_config()).sanitizer, so this pass compared bodies with CLOUD's fit while
  claiming to test DC." Note what did NOT happen: no exception, and the convergence assertion
  itself still passed — byte-identical output under both sanitizers, precisely as round 4(b)
  predicted. Only the recording check caught it.

MUTATED: dropped ONLY sanitizer= from the comment suite's `_diff`, keeping inbound_mapper=;
  FAILED: same test, same recording AssertionError. Confirms `_resolve_sanitizer` is an
  independent fallback and injecting the mapper does not cover it.

MUTATED: WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT 32767 -> 400000 (limit raised above the real ceiling);
  FAILED: test_dc_description_fit_is_a_plain_character_truncation — "assert 400000 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes — ceiling AssertionError;
  FAILED: test_dc_comment_fit_targets_the_documented_instance_ceiling — "assert 400000 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes — "The landed comment must carry the
  visible truncation marker …".

MUTATED: WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT -> 400000 with the earlier length/marker assertions neutralized,
  to prove the CONVERGENCE assertion is itself sensitive rather than shadowed;
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes — "Pass 2 must emit ZERO
  description updates (convergence)…";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes — "Pass 2 must emit ZERO comment
  mutations (convergence)…". This is the check the `_as_jira_would_store` addition bought.

MUTATED: WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound reduced to `return text` (fit removed);
  FAILED: test_dc_description_fit_is_a_plain_character_truncation — "assert 40000 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes — ceiling AssertionError;
  FAILED: test_dc_comment_fit_targets_the_documented_instance_ceiling — "assert 38015 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes — marker AssertionError.

NO PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. The sanitizer= seam (ticket 21ca) was sufficient, as the plan
said it would be; threading sanitizer through compute_outbound_mutations was NOT attempted and
remains a separate question. The limit was neither changed nor made configurable
(049e-9fac-a821-4ea2). The provenance comment cites jira.text.field.character.limit + jpm.xml's
default-value 32767 + JRASERVER-28519, plus the two known limits of the binding (admin-
configurability -> 049e-9fac; fit_outbound being the DESCRIPTION fitter) and a pointer to the new
comment suite.

BLOCKED ON A PRE-EXISTING MAIN FAILURE, NOT ON THIS CHANGE. Change 1234 cannot reach
Verified +1 because the gating `pip-audit` job is red on main. Filed as
[rebar:e47e-a33d-b9cf-4421] and linked discovered_from this story.

WHAT IS GREEN on change 1234 patchset 1: lint + type-check, verify-identity, require
resolvable rebar ticket, golden-path (clean install), optionality (both jobs),
artifact-probe, eval-discipline, clear Verified. The pytest matrix (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13
+ macos py3.13) was still running at the time of writing.

WHAT IS RED, and why it is not mine: `pip-audit` reports `click 8.2.1 PYSEC-2026-2132`
(fix version 8.3.3) — a command-injection advisory against `click.edit()`. `click` is a
TRANSITIVE dep pinned at 8.2.1 in the committed `uv.lock` (line 711); this story's diff is
two new test files plus a source comment and touches no dependency pin or manifest.
Reproduced identically on FIVE other patchset runs from other agents today (30770494611,
30770603146, 30770604307, 30770971365, 30771122330), all at head sha 4214516f95 — so it is
a property of main.

NOT RECHECKABLE. The job log shows the audit succeeded on attempt 1/3 — it REACHED the
advisory DB and found a real vulnerability. `_build-and-test.yml`'s failure policy reserves
`recheck` for the case where all three attempts fail to REACH the DB, so commenting
`recheck` would not clear this. It needs a lock refresh to click >= 8.3.3, or a justified
`--ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-2132`. Neither is in this story's file impact, and `uv.lock` is
plausibly contended with the agents working the uv-canonical lock change, so I did not
touch it.

Change 1234 is complete and ready otherwise; it needs e47e to land first (or an admin
override) before Submit. Not closing this ticket: per AGENTS.md a close requires the
change Verified +1 and merged, and neither holds yet.

compiled_state.description:
# DC comment/description length convergence — and settle whether the comment limit is even right

## Context

Cloud has two convergence suites that exist because oversized text caused real incidents:
`mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` and
`mutate/test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py`. Each drives an oversized value through
TWO passes and asserts the second plans nothing — i.e. the truncated value the adapter sent must
compare equal to what it reads back, or the differ re-emits the change forever.

**DC has neither.** And DC's comment path is the one with a question mark over it.

## The specific doubt, verified in source

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:146-149`:

    def sanitize_comment(self, body: str) -> str:
        return _shared_sanitize_comment(
            body, truncate=self._codec.fit_outbound, max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT
        )

Two things are bound to the DESCRIPTION here: the limit (`WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT`, 32767) and the
fitter (`fit_outbound`, the description fit). Cloud does not do this — it routes comments through a
dedicated `adapters/jira/comment_limits` module.

**RESOLVED — and the original suspicion here was WRONG, so this section is corrected rather than
left standing.** This story was written believing that whether 32767 is the correct DC comment
ceiling was UNKNOWN, and that Cloud's separate `comment_limits` module existed "precisely because
comment limits are not description limits". Both are now settled against primary sources:

* 32767 IS the correct DC comment ceiling for stock Jira >= 7.0 — it is the default of
  `jira.text.field.character.limit`, whose own definition covers "Description, Environment,
  **Comments** and Text custom fields". Comments and text custom fields are ONE property, so DC
  binding both to one constant is faithful to DC, not a shortcut.
* Cloud's `comment_limits` module exists because the UNITS differ, NOT the numbers: Cloud comments
  are limited in PLAIN characters (32767) while Cloud descriptions are limited in ADF-SERIALIZED
  size (`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` = 32000, fitted empirically because `text_to_adf` inflates — a
  32767-char description was measured serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars). DC has no ADF inflation,
  which is why one constant genuinely suffices there.

So the substance of this story is NOT "find out, then pin it". It is: add the two DC convergence
suites DC lacks, and cite the ceiling's provenance at the binding so the constant stops reading as
an assumption.

## Approach

1. THE CEILING IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED — do not re-measure it. Jira's own `jpm.xml` defines
   `jira.text.field.character.limit` with `default-value 32767` and a description covering
   "Description, Environment, **Comments** and Text custom fields", and JRASERVER-28519 records
   that 7.0.0 made 32767 the default. Comments and text custom fields are ONE property by design,
   so binding DC's comment limit to the same constant as its description limit is faithful to DC.
   The task is therefore to CITE that provenance in the source at the binding, so the constant
   reads as a decision rather than an assumption. Full evidence is in the research comment on this
   ticket. (That the limit is admin-configurable, and so wrong on a reconfigured instance, is a
   real but separate defect tracked as [rebar:049e-9fac-a821-4ea2]; it does NOT gate this story.)
2. Add the DC convergence suites as **SEPARATE FILES** in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/`.
   DO NOT parametrize them alongside Cloud's. Cloud's two suites hardcode Cloud-only internals
   that have no DC equivalent — `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`
   (`test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py:154`), and `ADF_PATH` /
   `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000` (`test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py:31-34`) —
   whereas DC fits via `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound`, a plain character truncation at
   `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT`, with no ADF serialization step at all. Parametrizing would require
   restructuring those incident-hardened Cloud tests, which this epic's own acceptance criteria
   forbid ("Cloud's pre-existing assertions still pass UNEDITED"). This mirrors the split that
   `cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e` names as its fallback; here the split is the DEFAULT, not the fallback,
   because the blocker is already known rather than something to discover by trying.
3. **INJECT THE DC BACKEND EXPLICITLY AT BOTH SEAMS. DO NOT DRIVE EITHER TEST THROUGH THE CONFIG
   FALLBACK — it silently resolves to CLOUD.** This is the single most important instruction in
   this plan and it was found by plan review, verified in source at 2ea5c3391d:
   * `compute_outbound_mutations` (`outbound_differ.py:382-391`) accepts `outbound_mapper`,
     `inbound_mapper` and `links` — but NO `sanitizer`. When any of the three is omitted it falls
     back to `select_backend(load_config())` (`outbound_differ.py:431-441`).
   * Worse for the COMMENT test: `outbound_differ.py:744-746` calls
     `_diff_comments(ticket, jira_key, comment_snapshot, client=client, inbound_mapper=inbound_mapper)`
     — it forwards NO `sanitizer`, so `_diff_comments` resolves one itself via
     `_resolve_sanitizer(None)` -> `select_backend(load_config()).sanitizer`
     (`outbound_comments.py:66-74, 205`), INDEPENDENTLY of any mapper the test injects.
   So a DC comment-convergence test driven through `compute_outbound_mutations` would compare
   bodies using CLOUD's sanitizer and converge against the WRONG truncation function — passing
   while proving nothing about DC. That is exactly the vacuous-green this epic exists to eliminate.
   THE REQUIRED SHAPES:
   * COMMENT convergence: call `_diff_comments(...)` DIRECTLY with an explicit
     `sanitizer=<the DC sanitizer>`. That keyword already exists (`outbound_comments.py:167`, the
     ticket-21ca injection seam) — no production change is needed to reach DC's path.
   * DESCRIPTION convergence: drive `compute_outbound_mutations` with ALL THREE of
     `outbound_mapper=`, `inbound_mapper=` and `links=` bound to a DC backend. Injecting only
     `outbound_mapper` is NOT enough: the guard at `outbound_differ.py:431` is an OR —
     `if outbound_mapper is None or inbound_mapper is None or links is None:` — so leaving ANY of
     the three unset fires the fallback block, which resolves the backend from config and can
     overwrite the others with CLOUD's. Construct a minimal `JiraDataCenterBackend` over a stub
     transport and pass `outbound_mapper=b.outbound, inbound_mapper=b.inbound, links=b`.
   NO PRODUCTION CHANGE IS IN SCOPE HERE. If threading `sanitizer` through
   `compute_outbound_mutations` looks desirable, that is a separate ticket, not this one.
3. Only then decide whether `max_chars` needs changing. A limit change is a BEHAVIOUR change and,
   if needed, belongs in its own bug ticket linked from here — not folded into a test story.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/` — NEW, DC-specific convergence files for comment and
  description. Cloud's two existing convergence files must be left BYTE-UNCHANGED.
- the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding in `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — a
  provenance COMMENT only, citing `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519.
- NOT the limit change itself, and NOT making the limit configurable (that is
  [rebar:049e-9fac-a821-4ea2]).

## Testing

Convergence is a two-pass property, so a single-pass assertion cannot establish it: the test must
run the pass twice and assert the SECOND plans nothing for that ticket. A first-pass-only test
would pass against a bridge that re-sends the same truncated comment forever.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] an oversized DC comment converges: pass 2 plans no further change for that ticket, asserted
      on the plan rather than on the absence of an exception
- [ ] an oversized DC description converges, same assertion shape
- [ ] the truncation suffix marker survives the round trip and is asserted, not just the length
- [ ] the DESCRIPTION test proves it exercised DC's fit by a VALUE-BASED discriminator: DC fits
      plain characters at `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32767), while Cloud fits ADF-SERIALIZED size at
      `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32000). Those genuinely differ, so a length/ADF-shape assertion here
      would FAIL if the fallback supplied Cloud's mapper
- [ ] the COMMENT test proves it exercised DC's sanitizer by an IDENTITY or RECORDING check, NOT by
      value. **A value-based discriminator is impossible here and must not be attempted**: DC's
      `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound` and Cloud's `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body` truncate at
      the SAME limit (32767 / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS`) and append a BYTE-IDENTICAL suffix
      (`" … [truncated by reconciler]"` — `rich_text.py:69` and `comment_limits.py:46`), computing
      `keep` the same way. Any assertion on the resulting string therefore passes under EITHER
      sanitizer and is a test that cannot fail. Instead capture the injected DC sanitizer and assert
      it is the one that ran — e.g. wrap it in a recorder and assert the recorder observed the call,
      or assert identity against `dc_backend.sanitizer`
- [ ] the comment test's mutation check targets the INJECTION, not the value: removing the explicit
      `sanitizer=` must turn the cell RED via the identity/recording check. (A value assertion could
      not detect that, which is precisely why the identity check is required.)
- [ ] the comment test injects `sanitizer=` into `_diff_comments` explicitly, and the description
      test injects ALL THREE of `outbound_mapper=`, `inbound_mapper=` and `links=`; neither relies
      on `select_backend(load_config())` for any of them
- [ ] mutation-checked for the injection itself: REMOVING the explicit injection (letting the
      config fallback resolve the backend) turns the DC cells RED rather than leaving them green —
      because a green-without-injection cell is testing Cloud while claiming to test DC
- [ ] the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding carries a source comment citing
      `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519, so a reader cannot mistake the 32767
      for an assumption — verified by reading the comment in the diff
- [ ] Cloud's two existing convergence files are BYTE-UNCHANGED (`git diff` shows no edit to
      `test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` or
      `test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py`), because the DC suites are separate files
